tests.title: Unit 2: Planning and Decision Making – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: A company decides in January that it will launch its new product only after assessing last year's sales and likely demand for the coming year. This step is part of:
options: Directing the sales team towards targets
Controlling the performance of the sales staff
Forecasting as the basis for planning

questions.question_text: "Planning is looking ahead" and "control is looking back" implies that:
options: Planning and control have no relation to each other
Control is performed before planning in all situations
Planning is forward-looking while control is a review of past performance
Both planning and control are concerned only with the future

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a limitation of planning?
options: It facilitates control by setting the standards of performance
It reduces the risk of uncertainty in the decisions taken by managers
It provides direction to the efforts of the people in an organisation
It may not work in a dynamic environment where conditions change quickly

questions.question_text: A firm prepares a plan to open 10 new outlets over five years. This is best described as:
A plan made for a one-time project, which is not likely to be repeated, is a:
Which among the following is a standing plan?
A hotel's rule that "all guests must be greeted within one minute of arrival" is best classified as:
Policies differ from rules in that policies:
options: Specify exactly what must be done with no scope for discretion
Give general guidelines for decision making and leave some discretion
Cover only the one-time activities of the organisation
Are framed by the lowest level of management alone

questions.question_text: A procedure is a:
options: Series of steps to be followed in a chronological order for a recurring task
Statement of what is allowed or not allowed in a particular situation
General guideline that is used to channel the thinking in decision making
Plan to be followed only for a one-time project of the organisation

questions.question_text: "No smoking in the factory premises" is a:
Which of the following describes a "method" as a type of plan?
options: The sequence of steps followed in the recruitment of the staff
A broad guideline for the delegation of authority in a firm
A plan for the construction of a new factory building in the town
The way in which a given task is to be performed, such as billing

questions.question_text: The plan which states the funds required for a specific project for the next year is a:
A strategy differs from a policy because a strategy:
options: Is only a guideline for the routine decisions of the lower levels
Is framed after decisions on the routine rules have been taken
Is a comprehensive plan to meet competition and the environment
Deals only with the internal working of a single department

questions.question_text: The first step in the planning process is:
Developing planning premises means:
options: Reviewing the results of the plans after they have been put into action
Choosing the best among several alternative courses of action available
Converting the plans into budgets and numerical targets
Establishing the assumptions about the future conditions in which plans will operate

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a step of the planning process that comes AFTER evaluating the alternatives?
The last step of the planning process is:
Derivative plans are the plans that:
options: Are made by the top management alone for the entire company
Are prepared only after the main plan has been completed in full
Support the main plan by covering its parts, like purchase and hiring
Replace the main plan when the main plan fails to meet its objectives

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of planning?
options: It promotes innovative ideas among the managers of the firm
It provides direction to the efforts of the people in the firm
It guarantees success of the firm under all conditions
It reduces the overlapping and wasteful activities in the firm

questions.question_text: Planning is a "primary function" because:
options: It precedes the other functions of management
It is a function that is performed once
It is the only function that is needed
It is performed by the owners alone

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a type of decision that is routine and repetitive?
Deciding to merge with a competitor is a:
Reordering stationery when stock falls to a minimum level is a:
Which of the following is characteristic of a strategic decision?
options: Routine, short-term, with little impact on the firm
Taken by the first-line supervisors at their discretion
Long-term, high-risk, with major impact on the organisation
Made by following a set of fixed rules and procedures

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a tactical (administrative) decision?
options: Allocation of the budget among departments of the firm
Choosing the markets in which the firm will operate
Deciding whether the firm should diversify into a new industry
Deciding the overall mission of the company

tests.title: Unit 2: Planning and Decision Making – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: An operating decision is generally taken by:
options: Lower-level managers on routine day-to-day matters
The Board of Directors in its quarterly meetings
Shareholders in the annual general meeting of the company
Top management, on long-term and risky issues of the firm

questions.question_text: The rational decision-making model assumes that the decision maker:
options: Takes decisions only on the basis of intuition
Has limited information and settles for any acceptable alternative
Has complete information and chooses the best alternative
Is influenced mainly by emotions and social pressure

questions.question_text: Herbert Simon's "bounded rationality" means that managers:
options: Take their decisions only on the basis of their emotions
Are fully rational and have perfect information at all times
Decide within the limits of their information and ability
Avoid taking decisions in all the situations of uncertainty

questions.question_text: "Satisficing" means:
options: Choosing an alternative that is good enough rather than the best
Rejecting all the alternatives that are available to the manager
Choosing the alternative that maximises the profit for the firm
Choosing the alternative which is cheapest for the firm

questions.question_text: Which step comes first in the decision-making process?
After a decision is implemented, the manager should:
options: Develop a new set of alternatives without checking the results
Delegate the matter to the shareholders of the company
Close the matter as the decision is final and cannot be changed
Follow up to check whether it is achieving the desired result

questions.question_text: Which of the following tools is used to evaluate alternatives by comparing the costs and benefits?
A decision tree helps a manager to:
options: Schedule the activities of a project on a time scale
Record the minutes of the meetings in the organisation
Map the alternatives and outcomes with their probabilities and payoffs
Draw the organisation structure of the firm in a hierarchy

questions.question_text: A decision matrix with probabilities gives the expected value. For a project with a 60% chance of a Rs 50 lakh profit and a 40% chance of a Rs 10 lakh loss, the expected value is:
Project A: 50% chance of Rs 80 lakh, 50% chance of Rs 0. Project B: sure profit of Rs 35 lakh. A risk-neutral manager using expected value would:
options: Choose B as its expected value is Rs 35 lakh
Be indifferent between the two projects
Choose A as its expected value is Rs 40 lakh

questions.question_text: SWOT analysis stands for:
In a SWOT analysis, "a competitor entering the market" is a:
In a SWOT analysis, "a highly skilled workforce" is a:
In a SWOT analysis, "a change in government policy that benefits the industry" is an:
The BCG matrix classifies business units by:
options: Market growth rate and relative market share
Profit margin and the cost of production
Level of technology and the age of the firm
Number of employees and the amount of capital

questions.question_text: In the BCG matrix, a business with a high market share in a low-growth market is a:
A business with a high market share in a high-growth market is called a:
A business with a low market share in a low-growth market is a:
A business unit with a low market share in a high-growth market is a:
Porter's generic strategies include:
A firm that offers low-priced products by cutting costs in all operations follows:
A firm that offers unique features and premium products valued by customers is following:
A strategy of serving a particular niche segment of the market is:
Porter's five forces model is used to analyse:
Which of the following is NOT one of Porter's five forces?

tests.title: Unit 2: Planning and Decision Making – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: A firm decides to keep its present strategy and continue serving the same customers with the same products. This is a:
Entering a new market with new products is called:
Selling more of the existing products in the existing markets is:
Selling the existing products in new markets is:
Launching new products in the existing market is:
A firm sells off a loss-making division to reduce its operations. This is:
MBO stands for:
The Gantt chart is a tool used for:
options: Evaluating decision alternatives by their payoffs

questions.question_text: PERT and CPM are techniques used for:
options: Planning and controlling the complex projects

questions.question_text: In a project network, the critical path is the:
options: Path with the greatest number of resources allotted to it
Path with the minimum cost of all the activities involved
Longest path, which fixes the minimum project time
Shortest path, which has the least number of activities

questions.question_text: If an activity on the critical path is delayed, the project completion time will:
options: Be reduced, because the other activities speed up
Remain the same, because of the available slack
Be delayed by the same amount
Not be affected, as the critical path changes at once

questions.question_text: Float or slack in a network refers to:
options: The time between the start and the end of the project
The time an activity can be delayed without delaying the project
The time taken by the critical activities of the project
The cost of the activities on the critical path

questions.question_text: An activity has earliest start 5, earliest finish 9, latest finish 12. The slack of this activity is:
Network paths: A-B-D takes 4+6+5 = 15 days; A-C-D takes 4+8+5 = 17 days. The project duration is:
In PERT, the expected time is computed as (O + 4M + P)/6. For O = 4, M = 6, P = 14, te is:
Forecasting differs from planning in that forecasting:
options: Predicts future conditions, while planning decides the course of action
Decides the course of action, while planning predicts the future
Is not required in any planning exercise
Is performed after the plans are executed

questions.question_text: Zero-based budgeting means that:
options: Budgets are prepared by adding a percentage to last year's figures
The budget for the year is fixed at zero for all departments
Only the capital expenditure is budgeted for the period
Every item of expense must be justified afresh in each budget period

questions.question_text: A flexible budget is one that:
options: Is prepared by the top management alone
Is fixed for the period and cannot be changed
Is prepared only for the sales of the firm
Can be adjusted to the actual level of activity

questions.question_text: A budget of Rs 2,00,000 is fixed for 10,000 units. If the actual activity is 12,000 units, a flexible budget for the variable costs of Rs 15 per unit would allow:
Which of these is a quantitative objective?
options: Improve the image of the firm

questions.question_text: Management by exception is a principle of:
options: Planning — managers set all the standards
Staffing — managers recruit only the exceptional people
Controlling — managers deal with major deviations only
Directing — managers motivate only the best employees

questions.question_text: The planning premises that are within the control of the organisation are called:
Which of these is an EXTERNAL planning premise?
Which of these is an example of a short-range plan?
options: The operating budget for the next quarter
The 5-year plan for the expansion of capacity
The 10-year plan to enter international markets
The vision statement of the firm

questions.question_text: "Plan A and, if it fails, Plan B for the same problem" shows planning's:
options: Lack of any forecast about the future events
Rigidity, through the fixed plans for the future
Dependence on the outsiders for the decisions

tests.title: Unit 2: Planning and Decision Making – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: Contingency planning involves:
options: Preparing a single plan which cannot be modified in the future
Avoiding forecasts of the future conditions altogether
Preparing alternative plans in case events do not go as expected
Waiting for a crisis to occur before preparing any plan for it

questions.question_text: A "programme" as a type of plan is:
options: A numerical statement of the expected income of the firm
A standing plan used for the repeated activities of the organisation
A rule laid down by the top management for all the employees
A single-use plan covering objectives, policies and resources for an undertaking

questions.question_text: The main difference between a programme and a project is that a project is:
options: A smaller and more specific part of a programme
A standing plan used again and again
The larger activity which includes many programmes
A plan that is made by the shareholders

questions.question_text: Opportunity cost in decision making refers to:
options: The cost already incurred in the decision
The value of the best alternative that is given up
The cost of implementing the decision
The cost that cannot be recovered

questions.question_text: Sunk costs should be:
options: Used to compute the profit of the decision
Added to the cost of the new alternative
Given the highest weight in decisions
Ignored in decisions about the future

questions.question_text: Groupthink in group decision making is the tendency of:
options: Members to give many different opinions on a subject
The leader to take decisions without consulting any member
Members to agree to preserve harmony instead of evaluating alternatives
Members to avoid attending the meetings of the group

questions.question_text: In the Delphi technique, the group members:
options: Are guided by the leader's opinion in all the rounds
Vote on the alternatives secretly in one round only
Meet face to face to discuss the problem in an open forum
Give their opinions anonymously in several rounds of questionnaires

questions.question_text: The key rule in brainstorming is that:
options: Criticism of ideas is withheld while the ideas are being generated
Only the practical ideas may be spoken in the session
Only the leader is allowed to suggest ideas to the group
Each idea is evaluated as soon as it has been put forward

questions.question_text: The nominal group technique involves:
options: Open discussion without any structure or any written ideas
Opinions being collected from outsiders by post or e-mail
The leader selecting the solution without a discussion
Writing ideas individually, then discussing and ranking them by vote

questions.question_text: Intuitive decision making relies on:
Which of the following is a feature of decision making?
options: It involves a choice among the alternatives
It is done only at the top level
It does not involve any risk

questions.question_text: Decision making is a "continuous process" because:
options: A single decision is enough for the whole life of the organisation
Managers keep making decisions on one problem or another all the time
Decisions are made only at the start of the year
Only the top management takes any decision

questions.question_text: A manager decides to pursue the course that gives the highest expected profit even though it carries some risk. The manager is:
The difference between planning and decision making is that:
options: Both are exactly the same in every respect of the process
Planning is a single step in the process of decision making
Decision making is the function of the lowest level alone
Decision making selects a course of action, one step in planning

questions.question_text: The "hierarchy of plans" runs from:
options: Policies to the mission and then to the budgets and rules
Mission to objectives, strategies, policies, procedures, rules and budgets
Budgets to the mission and then to the rules and policies
Rules to procedures, policies, strategies, objectives and mission

questions.question_text: A firm with Rs 10 crore turnover aims for Rs 12 crore next year. The expected growth target is:
If a firm sets an objective of 15% growth on sales of Rs 80 lakh, the target sales are:
The "SMART" objectives are those which are:
options: Standard, mechanical, automatic, regular and timed
Simple, modern, accurate, reliable and tested
Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound
Strategic, managed, assessed, recorded and traced

questions.question_text: The objective "to be the best in the industry" lacks which SMART criterion?
When a firm adopts a policy of promoting from within, it affects:
options: The budget for the purchase of materials
The procedure for the preparation of accounts

questions.question_text: The process of identifying the organisation's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats helps in:
Environmental scanning means:
options: Reviewing the internal accounts of the organisation each year
Cleaning the premises of the firm at periodic intervals
Scanning the documents of the applicants at the time of hiring
Monitoring the external environment for opportunities and threats

questions.question_text: PESTEL analysis examines:
options: Political, economic, social, technological, environmental and legal factors
Planning, execution, supervision, training, evaluation and learning
Profit, earnings, sales, targets, expenses and losses
People, equipment, stock, time, effort and leadership

questions.question_text: A firm that plans to merge with another to increase its market share is following:
Which of the following is true about planning?
options: It is concerned only with the past performance
It is performed only once at the time of the start
It is required only at the top level of the firm
It is pervasive, continuous and future-oriented
